evidence: Sall. Jug. 54.7: proelium male pugnātum (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Eun. 4.2.6: male sē habēre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The opposite of bene. Of health and mood it goes with habēre and esse: male sē habēre, to feel ill; male est animō, I feel unwell (Plaut. Curc. 2.3.33, Lewis & Short). With a verb of feeling it can mean “very much”: male metuō, I am badly afraid (Ter. Hec. 3.2.2, Lewis & Short). Before an adjective it often turns the sense round: male sānus, not in his right mind (Cic. Att. 9.15.5, Lewis & Short); male fīdus, not to be trusted.

sources: Lewis & Short: malus (male)
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 231.
